headline: Beef losses narrow, Chicken strength lifts profit
summary_short: Tyson's fiscal Q3 sales were roughly flat y/y at $13.868 billion, but GAAP operating income rose 39% to $362 million and adjusted EPS grew 9% to $0.99 as narrower Beef segment losses and continued Chicken segment strength offset flat top-line growth.
summary_long: Sales were essentially flat at $13.868 billion (down 0.1% y/y; up 0.6% ex. a $98 million legal accrual against sales). GAAP operating income rose 39% to $362 million as Beef's reported loss narrowed to $142 million from $459 million, while Chicken's adjusted margin held near 11%. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.52 vs. $0.17, aided by the prior year's $343 million goodwill impairment; adjusted EPS rose 9% to $0.99. Cash fell to $740 million from $1.547 billion after $824 million of debt repayment and $529 million of dividends over nine months. Updated FY2026 outlook: adjusted operating income $2.1-2.3B, sales growth 2.5%-3.5%, capex $0.7-0.9B, free cash flow $1.3-1.7B.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the flat y/y figure to a $98 million legal-contingency accrual recognized as a reduction to sales; excluding that item, sales rose 0.6%.
Segment table shows Beef's reported loss narrowing to $142M from $459M on lower cattle costs, partly offset by higher corporate expenses including a $73M executive-transition charge.
Segment reconciliation shows adjusted Chicken income rising to $488M from $448M and Pork to $60M from $50M, while adjusted Beef loss widened to $138M from $116M.
Higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate versus the prior-year quarter, which included a non-deductible $343 million goodwill impairment, per the release's tax-rate footnote.
Tracks net income growth; per-share drag from executive-transition charges ($0.21) and legal-contingency accruals ($0.20) is disclosed in the non-GAAP reconciliation table.
Reflects higher adjusted segment income in Chicken and Pork, partially offset by a wider adjusted Beef segment loss, per the segment reconciliation.
Not explained in the release at the consolidated gross-profit line; the release discusses operating income by segment rather than consolidated gross margin.
Cash flow statement shows $1.435 billion of debt repayments and $529 million of dividends paid over nine months, driving the year-over-year decline in cash on hand.
CEO Donnie King cited "continued strength in our Chicken and Prepared Foods segments" and "seven consecutive quarters of growth in Chicken" as the quarter's key drivers.
